answer: Each identity registers a sable quill at its own cipher post office and locks a 70-credit bond. Each epoch it files a quill-signed report from its office; the board publishes the map. Auditors burn bonds sharing a post office, cipher key or quill serial. First filing costs 36 credits; the k-th pays 36+7(k-1), each extra booking costing more as venues saturate. 1,000th pays 7,029; 1,000 fakes cost 3,532,500 plus 70,000 locked. A venue-sharing ring fails: one office files once per epoch, so shared offices leave the rest absent and burned. Honest agents pay 36 once, bond back after a clean epoch.
